title: Console entity-graph + usage fact cubes for multi-dimensional analytics
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Create a canonical, denormalized entity-graph layer and companion usage fact cubes to support fast, ad-hoc Console analytics and dashboards. This ticket covers schema design, ETL transforms, SCD strategy for entity dimensions (workspace, route, model_variant, user), and the curated star-schema tables that power cost/latency breakdowns, feature adoption funnels, and rollout / canary analytics.
acceptance_criteria: Produce entity dimension tables: dim_workspace, dim_route, dim_model_variant, dim_user with stable surrogate keys and SCD-2 history for name/owner changes
Materialize usage fact cube: fact_console_usage with per-invocation metrics (tokens, latency_ms, cost_estimate, route_id, variant_id, workspace_id, user_id) partitioned by date and hour
ETL job(s) run end-to-end in CI for a synthetic 7-day dataset and validate row counts and key joins within 48h
Query performance: common dashboard queries (30-day workspace cost rollup, 7-day route latency p95) return in <3s on BI cluster using created materialized views
Backfill strategy documented and automated: fast-path daily incremental + bounded backfill for first 90 days
Data contracts documented and linked; owners assigned for each dimension and fact
Integration smoke tests added to pipeline that assert referential integrity and SLO for delayed events (<1% late beyond 1hr window)
Dashboards updated to reference new curated tables and validated by PM and Analytics SME
notes: Motivation: current console dashboards run many heavy joins against raw event stream; this causes high query cost and variable latency for product analytics and for customer-facing billing reconciliations.

Goal: provide an intermediate curated layer that balances normalization for correctness and denormalization for query speed. Primary consumers: product analytics, Console frontend, Cost engineering, Support. Secondary: SRE for incident forensics.
Trade-offs considered: full denormalization (single flattened table) vs star schema. Chosen star schema allows incremental refresh and SCD handling without reprocessing entire dataset.

Storage impact estimate: additional 1.8x storage for curated layer, but expected 4-6x reduction in query cost for common ops. We will aggressively TTL older hourly partitions for unused granularities after 1 year.
technical_design: - dim_workspace: surrogate workspace_key (int), workspace_id (string), name, org_id, plan_tier, created_at, current_flag, effective_from, effective_to
- dim_route: surrogate route_key, route_id, route_type, owner_team, public_flag, tags, effective_from/effective_to
- dim_model_variant: surrogate variant_key, model_name, quantization_profile, compiled_kernels_hash, runtime_compatibility_tags
- dim_user: surrogate user_key, user_id, email_hash (pseudonymized), role, workspace_key
SCD strategy: implement SCD-2 with surrogate keys for dim tables. Use event_time and entity_change_events topic to drive dimension deltas. Compact historical snapshots daily.

Fact table: fact_console_usage columns: event_date, event_hour, usage_id (uuid), workspace_key, route_key, variant_key, user_key, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, error_flag, cost_cents_estimate, request_tags (denormed json string), ingestion_timestamp

Partitioning & clustering: partition fact by event_date, cluster by (workspace_key, route_key) to improve common rollups. Keep hourly partitions for 7 days then rollup to daily granularity table for long-term retention.
Idempotency and dedup: use (usage_id) primary dedup key; pipeline will use dedupe windows with watermarking and housekeeping to remove late dups.

Backfill approach: use snapshot-based backfill for first 60 days, then change-data extraction for older ranges. Implement parallelized backfill with throttling to avoid impact on production warehouse.
Metrics & monitoring: create SLIs for ETL freshness, partition creation success rate, join referential integrity failures; publish to Console Observability channels.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design & review): finish schema, peer review with analytics and product (1 week)
Phase 1 (pilot): implement ETL for dim_workspace and fact_console_usage for 7-day window; run queries for two pilot dashboards and compare with canonical metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (expand): add dim_route, dim_model_variant, dim_user; extend backfill to 90 days; update dashboards and queries to point to curated tables (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (cutover): make dashboards and BI ETL read only from curated tables; keep raw event stream available for forensic joins; deprecate expensive joins by tagging older queries (1 week)
Rollback plan: retain last consistent snapshot; provide views that map old raw column names to curated schema for fallback; maintain retention of raw events for 30 days post-cutover
test_plan: Unit tests for transform logic (key mapping, SCD generation, cost computation)
Integration tests: run end-to-end on staging with synthetic traffic generator (include error cases and late-arriving events)
Performance tests: run typical dashboard queries against BI cluster, measure p50/p95 and compare with baseline
Data quality checks: referential integrity checks, duplicate detection, null-rate thresholds, and distribution drift alerts
